t: Data Lineage Tracker: a plain-language overview
title: Data Lineage Tracker: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Data Lineage Tracker does and why archives need it. A data lineage tracker remembers the life story of every data item: where it came from, what was done to it, and what it became. Raw survey answers became cleaned tables became published charts — the tracker records each step. Any number can be traced back to its source, step by step.
demo:
# Data Lineage Tracker - runnable demo (JAH-ATK189-000001)
from collections import defaultdict, deque
RANK = 1
SIG = False
TRANSFORMS = [('cleaned', ['raw'], 'dedupe'), ('stats', ['cleaned'], 'aggregate'), ('report', ['stats'], 'render')]  # (output, [inputs], operation)
children = defaultdict(list); parents = {}
for out, ins, op in TRANSFORMS:
    parents[out] = (ins, op)
    for i in ins: children[i].append(out)
def trace_back(node):
    chain, q = [], deque([node])
    seen = set()
    while q:
        n = q.popleft()
        if n in seen: continue
        seen.add(n); chain.append(n)
        ins, _ = parents.get(n, ([], None))
        q.extend(ins)
    return chain
TARGET = TRANSFORMS[-1][0]
print("lineage of", TARGET, ":")
for n in trace_back(TARGET):
    ins, op = parents.get(n, ([], "SOURCE"))
    print("  %-12s <- %s [%s]" % (n, ins if ins else "-", op))
if RANK >= 2:
    affected = [c for c in children[TRANSFORMS[0][1][0]]]
    print("downstream of source:", affected)
if RANK >= 3:
    print("transformations logged:", len(TRANSFORMS))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-LIN-" + "JAH-ATK189-000001")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK189-000001", "OK")

t: How the Data Lineage Tracker works
title: How the Data Lineage Tracker works

Real trackers log every transformation as a directed acyclic graph (DAG): source datasets are roots, operations (filter, join, aggregate) are nodes, and derived datasets are leaves, each edge stamped with the operation, its parameters, and its timestamp. t: How the Data Lineage Tracker works: the deep tour
title: How the Data Lineage Tracker works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Data Lineage Tracker does and why archives need it. Real trackers log every transformation as a directed acyclic graph (DAG): source datasets are roots, operations (filter, join, aggregate) are nodes, and derived datasets are leaves, each edge stamped with the operation, its parameters, and its timestamp. Column-level lineage tracks individual fields through renames and derivations. When a source is corrected, the tracker walks the DAG forward to find every downstream product that must be rebuilt. Advanced systems capture lineage automatically by instrumenting query engines and ETL frameworks, verify completeness by reconciling logged transforms against actual outputs, and handle streaming data with windowed lineage. Quality is measured by trace completeness on audited pipelines. The limits are manual spreadsheet edits and untracked ad-hoc queries — the tracker marks products with lineage gaps honestly rather than claiming a complete chain it does not have.

Real trackers log every transformation as a directed acyclic graph (DAG): source datasets are roots, operations (filter, join, aggregate) are nodes, and derived datasets are leaves, each edge stamped with the operation, its parameters, and its timestamp.
